f.title: Make the 314.81 postmarketing reports for every approved NDA and ANDA
f.statement: Each applicant shall make the reports required under 314.81 and section 505(k) of the act for each of its approved applications and abbreviated applications.

rows.quote:
(a) Applicability. Each applicant shall
make the reports for each of its approved applications and abbreviated
applications required under this section and section 505(k) of the act.

f.title: Submit two copies of each 314.81 report at the specified times
f.statement: The applicant shall submit to FDA, at the specified times, two copies of the reports listed in 314.81(b).

f.title: Submit NDA Field Alert Reports to the responsible FDA district office within 3 working days of receipt
f.statement: The applicant shall submit field alert information about distributed drug products and articles to the FDA district office responsible for the facility involved within 3 working days of receipt by the applicant.

rows.deadline: Within 3 working days of receipt by the applicant
rows.quote:
products and articles to the FDA district office that is responsible for the
facility involved within 3 working days
of receipt by the applicant.

deadline_rule.applies_to: NDA Field Alert Reports (product mix-ups, contamination, deterioration, specification failures)

f.title: Field alert information may be given by telephone or other rapid means with prompt written follow-up
f.statement: Field alert information may be provided by telephone or other rapid communication means, with prompt written followup.

rows.quote:
The information may be provided by telephone
or other rapid communication means,
with prompt written followup.

f.title: Mark the field alert report and its mailing cover "NDA-Field Alert Report"
f.statement: The report and its mailing cover should be plainly marked "NDA-Field Alert Report."

rows.quote:
The report and its mailing cover should be
plainly marked: ‘‘NDA—Field Alert Report.’’

f.title: Report any incident causing the drug or its labeling to be mistaken for or applied to another article
f.statement: The field alert report shall include information concerning any incident that causes the drug product or its labeling to be mistaken for, or applied to, another article.

rows.quote:
(i) Information concerning any incident that causes the drug product or
its labeling to be mistaken for, or applied to, another article.

f.title: Report contamination, significant change or deterioration, or specification failure of distributed batches
f.statement: The field alert report shall include information concerning any bacteriological contamination, or any significant chemical, physical or other change or deterioration in the distributed drug product, or any failure of one or more distributed batches to meet the specification established in the application.

rows.quote:
(ii) Information concerning any bacteriological contamination, or any significant chemical, physical, or other
change or deterioration in the distributed drug product, or any failure of one
or more distributed batches of the drug
product to meet the specification established for it in the application.

f.title: Submit the annual report within 60 days of the U.S. approval anniversary date
f.statement: The applicant shall submit each year, within 60 days of the anniversary date of U.S. approval of the application, two copies of the annual report to the FDA division responsible for reviewing the application.

rows.deadline: Each year within 60 days of the anniversary date of U.S. approval
rows.quote:
(2) Annual report. The applicant shall
submit each year within 60 days of the
anniversary date of U.S. approval of
the application, two copies of the report to the FDA division responsible
for reviewing the application.

deadline_rule.clock_start: the anniversary date of U.S. approval of the application

f.title: Accompany the annual report with Form FDA 2252 and cover the full reporting interval in the listed order
f.statement: Each annual report must be accompanied by a completed transmittal Form FDA 2252 and must include all information required under 314.81 that the applicant received or otherwise obtained during the annual reporting interval ending on the U.S. anniversary date, in the order listed.

rows.quote:
Each annual report is required to be accompanied by a completed transmittal
Form FDA 2252 (Transmittal of Periodic Reports for Drugs for Human Use),
and must include all the information
required under this section that the applicant received or otherwise obtained
during the annual reporting interval
that ends on the U.S. anniversary date.
The report is required to contain in the
order listed:

f.title: Summarise significant new safety, effectiveness or labeling information from the previous year
f.statement: The annual report must contain a brief summary of significant new information from the previous year that might affect the safety, effectiveness or labeling of the drug product.

rows.quote:
(i) Summary. A brief summary of significant new information from the previous year that might affect the safety,
effectiveness, or labeling of the drug
product.

f.title: Describe the actions taken or planned in response to the new information
f.statement: The annual report must also contain a brief description of actions the applicant has taken or intends to take as a result of the new information, for example submitting a labeling supplement, adding a warning to the labeling, or initiating a new study.

rows.quote:
The report is also required to
contain a brief description of actions
the applicant has taken or intends to
take as a result of this new information, for example, submit a labeling
supplement, add a warning to the labeling, or initiate a new study.

f.title: State whether pediatric labeling supplements were submitted and pediatric studies initiated
f.statement: The summary shall briefly state whether labeling supplements for pediatric use have been submitted and whether new studies in the pediatric population to support appropriate labeling have been initiated.

rows.quote:
The summary shall briefly state whether labeling supplements for pediatric use have
been submitted and whether new studies in the pediatric population to support appropriate labeling for the pediatric population have been initiated.

f.title: Estimate patient exposure, with special reference to the pediatric population, where possible
f.statement: Where possible, an estimate of patient exposure to the drug product, with special reference to the pediatric population (neonates, infants, children and adolescents), shall be provided, including dosage form.

rows.quote:
Where possible, an estimate of patient
exposure to the drug product, with special reference to the pediatric popu-

lation (neonates, infants, children, and
adolescents) shall be provided, including dosage form.
rows.review_note: Template gaps 2026-11-23, extractor. Quote crosses a column break.

f.title: Report quantities distributed, by NDC, strength and domestic or foreign use
f.statement: The annual report must include information about the quantity of the drug product distributed under the approved application, including to distributors: the NDC number, the total number of dosage units of each strength or potency distributed, and the quantities distributed for domestic and for foreign use; financial or pricing data are not required.

rows.quote:
(ii)(a) Distribution data. Information
about the quantity of the drug product
distributed under the approved application, including that distributed to distributors. The information is required
to include the National Drug Code
(NDC) number, the total number of
dosage units of each strength or potency distributed (e.g., 100,000/5 milligram tablets, 50,000/10 milliliter vials),
and the quantities distributed for domestic use and the quantities distributed for foreign use. Disclosure of financial or pricing data is not required.

f.title: Report authorized generic market entry and exit dates and brand names
f.statement: If applicable, the annual report must give the date each authorized generic drug entered the market, the date it ceased being distributed and the corresponding trade or brand name; each dosage form and/or strength is a different authorized generic and should be listed separately.

rows.quote:
(b) Authorized generic drugs. If applicable, the date each authorized generic
drug (as defined in § 314.3) entered the
market, the date each authorized generic drug ceased being distributed,
and the corresponding trade or brand
name. Each dosage form and/or
strength is a different authorized generic drug and should be listed separately.

f.title: Backfill authorized generic data since 1999 in the first annual report on or after 25 January 2010
f.statement: The first annual report submitted on or after January 25, 2010 must include the authorized generic information for any authorized generic drug marketed during the period covered by an annual report submitted after January 1, 1999.

rows.quote:
The first annual report submitted on or after January 25, 2010
must include the information listed in
this paragraph for any authorized generic drug that was marketed during
the time period covered by an annual
report submitted after January 1, 1999.
rows.review_note: Template gaps 2026-11-23, extractor. Historical one-off requirement; not recorded as a document date.

f.title: Send a copy of the authorized generic portion of the annual report to CDER
f.statement: If the annual report includes information on any authorized generic drug, a copy of that portion must be sent to CDER's Office of New Drug Quality Assessment marked "Authorized Generic Submission", or by e-mail to the Authorized Generics mailbox with that subject line; once FDA requires electronic annual reports, the information must instead be submitted as part of the electronic annual report.
f.exceptions: When FDA requires electronic annual reports, submit within the electronic annual report instead of separately

rows.quote:
If information is included in the annual
report with respect to any authorized
generic drug, a copy of that portion of
the annual report must be sent to the
Food and Drug Administration, Center
for Drug Evaluation and Research, Office of New Drug Quality Assessment,
rows.review_note: Template gaps 2026-11-23, extractor. Quote stops before the postal address and mailbox address.

f.title: Include currently used labeling and package label samples in the annual report
f.statement: The annual report must include currently used professional labeling, patient brochures or package inserts (if any), and a representative sample of the package labels.

rows.quote:
(iii) Labeling. (a) Currently used professional labeling, patient brochures or
package inserts (if any), and a representative sample of the package labels.

f.title: Submit the package insert content in an FDA-processable electronic format under part 11
f.statement: The content of labeling required under 201.100(d)(3) (package insert or professional labeling), including all text, tables and figures, must be submitted in an electronic format FDA can process, review and archive, in accordance with part 11 except 11.10(a), (c) through (h) and (k) and the corresponding requirements of 11.30.

rows.quote:
(b) The content of labeling required
under § 201.100(d)(3) of this chapter (i.e.,
the package insert or professional labeling), including all text, tables, and
figures, must be submitted in electronic format. Electronic format submissions must be in a form that FDA
can process, review, and archive. FDA
will periodically issue guidance on how
to provide the electronic submission
(e.g., method of transmission, media,
file formats, preparation and organization of files). Submissions under this
paragraph must be made in accordance
with part 11 of this chapter, except for
the requirements of § 11.10(a), (c)
through (h), and (k), and the corresponding requirements of § 11.30.

f.title: Summarise labeling changes since the last report, by date
f.statement: The annual report must include a summary of any changes in labeling made since the last report, listed by date in the order implemented, or a statement that there were no changes.

rows.quote:
(c) A summary of any changes in labeling that have been made since the
last report listed by date in the order
in which they were implemented, or if
no changes, a statement of that fact.

f.title: Report new CMC experiences, investigations or tests that may affect safety or effectiveness conclusions
f.statement: The annual report must include reports of experiences, investigations, studies or tests involving chemical, physical or other properties of the drug (including its behavior in relation to microorganisms), required only for new information that may affect FDA's previous conclusions about the safety or effectiveness of the drug product.

rows.quote:
(iv) Chemistry, manufacturing, and
controls changes. (a) Reports of experiences, investigations, studies, or tests
involving chemical or physical properties, or any other properties of the
drug (such as the drug’s behavior or
properties in relation to microorganisms, including both the effects of the
drug on microorganisms and the effects
of microorganisms on the drug). These
reports are only required for new information that may affect FDA’s previous
conclusions about the safety or effectiveness of the drug product.

f.title: Describe manufacturing and controls changes not needing a supplement, by date
f.statement: The annual report must include a full description of the manufacturing and controls changes not requiring a supplemental application under 314.70(b) and (c), listed by date in the order implemented.

rows.quote:
(b) A full description of the manufacturing and controls changes not requiring a supplemental application under
§ 314.70 (b) and (c), listed by date in the
order in which they were implemented.

f.title: Report new toxicological findings from animal and in vitro studies
f.statement: The annual report must include copies of unpublished reports and summaries of published reports of new toxicological findings in animal and in vitro studies (e.g. mutagenicity) conducted or otherwise obtained by the applicant concerning the ingredients in the drug product.

rows.quote:
(v) Nonclinical laboratory studies. Copies of unpublished reports and summaries of published reports of new toxicological findings in animal studies
and in vitro studies (e.g., mutagenicity) conducted by, or otherwise obtained by, the applicant concerning the
ingredients in the drug product.

f.title: Submit a copy of a published nonclinical report if FDA requests it
f.statement: The applicant shall submit a copy of a published nonclinical report if requested by FDA.

rows.quote:
The
applicant shall submit a copy of a published report if requested by FDA.

f.title: Report published clinical trials and clinical experience pertinent to safety
f.statement: The annual report must include published clinical trials of the drug (or abstracts), including trials on safety and effectiveness and on new uses, biopharmaceutic, pharmacokinetic and clinical pharmacology studies, and reports of clinical experience pertinent to safety (e.g. epidemiologic studies or analyses of experience in a monitored series of patients) conducted or otherwise obtained by the applicant.

rows.quote:
(vi) Clinical data. (a) Published clinical trials of the drug (or abstracts of

them), including clinical trials on safety and effectiveness; clinical trials on
new uses; biopharmaceutic, pharmacokinetic, and clinical pharmacology
studies; and reports of clinical experience pertinent to safety (for example,
epidemiologic studies or analyses of experience in a monitored series of patients) conducted by or otherwise obtained by the applicant.
rows.review_note: Template gaps 2026-11-23, extractor. Quote crosses a column break.

f.title: Do not report review articles, practice papers, research-tool papers, promotional articles or press clippings
f.statement: Review articles, papers describing use of the drug in medical practice, papers and abstracts using the drug as a research tool, promotional articles, press clippings and papers without tabulations or summaries of original data should not be reported.

rows.quote:
Review articles, papers describing the use of the
drug product in medical practice, papers and abstracts in which the drug is
used as a research tool, promotional
articles, press clippings, and papers
that do not contain tabulations or
summaries of original data should not
be reported.

f.title: Summarise completed unpublished clinical trials
f.statement: The annual report must include summaries of completed unpublished clinical trials, or prepublication manuscripts if available, conducted or otherwise obtained by the applicant; a study is considered completed 1 year after it is concluded.

rows.quote:
(b) Summaries of completed unpublished clinical trials, or prepublication
manuscripts if available, conducted by,
or otherwise obtained by, the applicant.

f.title: Do not report supporting information for unpublished trials; treat a study as completed 1 year after it concludes
f.statement: Supporting information for unpublished clinical trial summaries should not be reported; a study is considered completed 1 year after it is concluded.

rows.quote:
Supporting information should
not be reported. (A study is considered
completed 1 year after it is concluded.)

f.title: Analyse pediatric safety and efficacy data and assess the data needed for pediatric labeling
f.statement: The annual report must include an analysis of available safety and efficacy data in the pediatric population and changes proposed in the labeling based on this information, and shall include an assessment of data needed to ensure appropriate labeling for the pediatric population.

rows.quote:
(c) Analysis of available safety and
efficacy data in the pediatric population and changes proposed in the labeling based on this information. An
assessment of data needed to ensure
appropriate labeling for the pediatric
population shall be included.

f.title: Report the status of each required or committed postmarketing study
f.statement: The annual report must include a status report of each postmarketing study of the drug product concerning clinical safety, clinical efficacy, clinical pharmacology and nonclinical toxicology that is required by FDA (e.g. accelerated approval clinical benefit studies, pediatric studies) or that the applicant has committed in writing to conduct, at or after approval of an application or supplement.

rows.quote:
(vii) Status reports of postmarketing
study commitments. A status report of
each postmarketing study of the drug
product concerning clinical safety,
clinical efficacy, clinical pharmacology, and nonclinical toxicology that
is required by FDA (e.g., accelerated
approval clinical benefit studies, pediatric studies) or that the applicant has
committed, in writing, to conduct either at the time of approval of an application for the drug product or a supplement to an application, or after approval of the application or a supplement.

f.title: State whether pediatric postmarketing studies were required under 201.23
f.statement: For pediatric studies, the status report shall include a statement indicating whether postmarketing clinical studies in pediatric populations were required by FDA under 201.23.

rows.quote:
For pediatric studies, the status
report shall include a statement indicating whether postmarketing clinical
studies in pediatric populations were
required by FDA under § 201.23 of this
chapter.

f.title: Report postmarketing study status annually until FDA concurs the commitment is fulfilled or moot
f.statement: The status of these postmarketing studies shall be reported annually until FDA notifies the applicant in writing that it concurs with the applicant's determination that the study commitment has been fulfilled or that the study is no longer feasible or would no longer provide useful information.

rows.deadline: Annually, until FDA concurs in writing
rows.quote: The status of these postmarketing studies shall be reported annually until FDA notifies the applicant, in writing, that the agency concurs with the applicant’s determination that the study commitment has
rows.review_note: Template gaps 2026-11-23, extractor. Quote ends at "commitment has"; the rest ("been fulfilled or ... no longer provide useful information") follows a page break. SME review 2026-11-24: stays held (quote stops at a page break); statement revised.

f.title: Give applicant, product, application, approval and commitment identification for each postmarketing study
f.statement: For each postmarketing study the status report must provide the applicant's name; product name (established and proprietary); NDA, ANDA and supplement number; date of U.S. approval; date of the commitment; and a description of the commitment with enough information to uniquely describe the study.

rows.quote:
(a) Content of status report. The following information must be provided
for each postmarketing study reported
under this paragraph:
(1) Applicant’s name.
(2) Product name. Include the approved drug product’s established name
and proprietary name, if any.
(3) NDA, ANDA, and supplement number.
(4) Date of U.S. approval of NDA or
ANDA.
(5) Date of postmarketing study commitment.
(6) Description of postmarketing study
commitment. The description must include sufficient information to uniquely describe the study. This information
may include the purpose of the study,
the type of study, the patient population addressed by the study and the
indication(s) and dosage(s) that are to
be studied.

f.title: Give the completion and reporting schedule, including any revised schedule
f.statement: The status report should include the schedule for completion and reporting of the commitment, with actual or projected dates for protocol submission, completion of patient accrual or initiation of an animal study, study completion, final study report submission and other committed milestones, plus a revised schedule as appropriate; if previously revised, both the original schedule and the most recent revision.

rows.quote:
(7) Schedule for completion and reporting of the postmarketing study commitment. The schedule should include the
actual or projected dates for submission of the study protocol to FDA,
completion of patient accrual or initiation of an animal study, completion of
the study, submission of the final
study report to FDA, and any additional milestones or submissions for
which projected dates were specified as
part of the commitment. In addition, it
should include a revised schedule, as
appropriate. If the schedule has been
previously revised, provide both the
original schedule and the most recent,
previously submitted revision.
rows.review_note: Template gaps 2026-11-23, extractor. SME review 2026-11-24: amendment 6 of 89 FR 105288 adds only (b)(3)(v), so this 4-1-25 text is current for this row; confirmed. Review: Mandatory, because item (7) is in the 'must be provided' list; 'should' shapes only the schedule detail.

f.title: Categorise each study as pending, ongoing, delayed, terminated or submitted
f.statement: The status of each postmarketing study should be categorized on the U.S. approval anniversary date (or other agreed date) as Pending, Ongoing, Delayed, Terminated or Submitted, as defined in 314.81(b)(2)(vii)(a)(8).

rows.quote:
(8) Current status of the postmarketing
study commitment. The status of each
postmarketing study should be categorized using one of the following
terms that describes the study’s status
on the anniversary date of U.S. approval of the application or other
agreed upon date:
(i) Pending. The study has not been
initiated, but does not meet the criterion for delayed.
(ii) Ongoing. The study is proceeding
according to or ahead of the original
schedule described under paragraph
(b)(2)(vii)(a)(7) of this section.

(iii) Delayed. The study is behind the
original schedule described under paragraph (b)(2)(vii)(a)(7) of this section.
(iv) Terminated. The study was ended
before completion but a final study report has not been submitted to FDA.
(v) Submitted. The study has been
completed or terminated and a final
study report has been submitted to
FDA.
rows.review_note: Template gaps 2026-11-23, extractor. Quote crosses a column break.

f.title: Explain each study's status, accrual, completion dates and any schedule revision
f.statement: The status report must provide a brief description of the study's status, including the patient accrual rate (number enrolled to date and total planned) and an explanation of the status category; if completed, the completion date and final study report submission date; and a revised schedule with reasons if the schedule has changed since the last report.

rows.quote:
(9) Explanation of the study’s status.
Provide a brief description of the status of the study, including the patient
accrual rate (expressed by providing
the number of patients or subjects enrolled to date, and the total planned
enrollment), and an explanation of the
study’s status identified under paragraph (b)(2)(vii)(a)(8) of this section. If
the study has been completed, include
the date the study was completed and
the date the final study report was submitted to FDA, as applicable. Provide a
revised schedule, as well as the reason(s) for the revision, if the schedule
under paragraph (b)(2)(vii)(a)(7) of this
section has changed since the last report.

f.title: Report the status of other postmarketing studies performed by or for the applicant
f.statement: The annual report must include a status report of any postmarketing study not included under 314.81(b)(2)(vii) that is being performed by, or on behalf of, the applicant.

rows.quote:
(viii) Status of other postmarketing
studies. A status report of any postmarketing study not included under
paragraph (b)(2)(vii) of this section
that is being performed by, or on behalf
of, the applicant.

f.title: Report the status of agreed CMC studies and all product stability studies
f.statement: A status report is to be included for any chemistry, manufacturing and controls studies the applicant has agreed to perform and for all product stability studies.

rows.quote:
A status report is to
be included for any chemistry, manufacturing, and controls studies that the
applicant has agreed to perform and for
all product stability studies.

f.title: Optionally include a log of outstanding regulatory business
f.statement: At the applicant's discretion, the annual report may also contain a list of any open regulatory business with FDA concerning the drug product (e.g. unanswered correspondence either way).

rows.quote:
(ix) Log of outstanding regulatory business. To facilitate communications between FDA and the applicant, the report may, at the applicant’s discretion,
also contain a list of any open regulatory business with FDA concerning
the drug product subject to the application (e.g., a list of the applicant’s unanswered correspondence with the
agency, a list of the agency’s unanswered correspondence with the applicant).

f.title: Submit promotional labeling and advertisements at first dissemination or publication
f.statement: The applicant shall submit specimens of mailing pieces and any other labeling or advertising devised for promotion of the drug product at the time of initial dissemination of the labeling and at the time of initial publication of the advertisement for a prescription drug product.

rows.quote:
(3) Other reporting—(i) Advertisements
and promotional labeling. The applicant
shall submit specimens of mailing
pieces and any other labeling or advertising devised for promotion of the
drug product at the time of initial dissemination of the labeling and at the
time of initial publication of the advertisement for a prescription drug product.

f.title: Submit sample-containing mailing pieces complete, except the drug sample
f.statement: Mailing pieces and labeling designed to contain samples of a drug product are required to be complete, except that the sample may be omitted.

rows.quote:
Mailing pieces and labeling that
are designed to contain samples of a
drug product are required to be complete, except the sample of the drug
product may be omitted.

f.title: Accompany promotional submissions with Form FDA-2253 and the current professional labeling
f.statement: Each promotional submission must be accompanied by a completed transmittal Form FDA-2253 and include a copy of the product's current professional labeling.

rows.quote:
Each submission is required to be accompanied by a
completed transmittal Form FDA–2253
(Transmittal of Advertisements and
Promotional Labeling for Drugs for
Human Use) and is required to include
a copy of the product’s current professional labeling.

f.title: Submit 314.81 reports at different times when FDA requires it in writing
f.statement: When FDA requires it by written request, the applicant must submit the 314.81 reports at the different times FDA states.

rows.quote:
(ii) Special reports. Upon written request the agency may require that the
applicant submit the reports under this
section at different times than those
stated.

f.title: Notify FDA of a permanent discontinuance or meaningful manufacturing interruption of a critical prescription drug
f.statement: An applicant of a prescription drug product must notify FDA in writing of a permanent discontinuance of manufacture, or an interruption in manufacturing likely to lead to a meaningful disruption in U.S. supply, if the drug is life supporting, life sustaining or intended for use in preventing or treating a debilitating disease or condition (including emergency medical care or surgery) and is not a radiopharmaceutical.
f.applicability: Prescription drug products that are life supporting, life sustaining or intended to prevent or treat a debilitating disease or condition (including emergency or surgical use), other than radiopharmaceuticals

rows.actor: Applicant of a prescription drug product
rows.quote:
(iii) Notification of a permanent discontinuance or an interruption in manufacturing. (a) An applicant of a prescription drug product must notify
FDA in writing of a permanent discontinuance of manufacture of the
drug product or an interruption in
manufacturing of the drug product
that is likely to lead to a meaningful
disruption in supply of that drug in the
United States if:
(1) The drug product is life supporting, life sustaining, or intended for
use in the prevention or treatment of a
debilitating disease or condition, including any such drug used in emergency medical care or during surgery;
and

(2) The drug product is not a radiopharmaceutical drug product.

f.title: Submit discontinuance or interruption notifications electronically at least 6 months in advance
f.statement: Notifications required by 314.81(b)(3)(iii)(a) must be submitted to FDA electronically in a format FDA can process, review and archive at least 6 months prior to the date of the permanent discontinuance or interruption in manufacturing.

f.title: If 6 months' notice is not possible, notify as soon as practicable and within 5 business days
f.statement: If 6 months' advance notice is not possible because the permanent discontinuance or interruption was not reasonably anticipated 6 months in advance, the notification must be submitted as soon as practicable thereafter, but in no case later than 5 business days after the discontinuance or interruption occurs.
f.applicability: Prescription drug products that are life supporting, life sustaining or intended to prevent or treat a debilitating disease or condition (including emergency or surgical use), other than radiopharmaceuticals

f.title: Include drug, NDC, applicant, type, reason and expected duration in the notification
f.statement: Discontinuance or interruption notifications must include the drug name and NDC, the applicant name, whether it concerns a permanent discontinuance or an interruption, a description of the reason, and the estimated duration of the interruption.

include the following information:
(1) The name of the drug subject to
the notification, including the NDC for
such drug;
(2) The name of the applicant;
(3) Whether the notification relates
to a permanent discontinuance of the
drug or an interruption in manufacturing of the drug;
(4) A description of the reason for the
permanent discontinuance or interruption in manufacturing; and
(5) The estimated duration of the
interruption in manufacturing.

f.title: Respond within 30 calendar days to an FDA letter on a missed shortage notification
f.statement: If FDA issues a letter for failure to submit a required notification, the applicant must, not later than 30 calendar days after issuance of the letter, submit a written response setting forth the basis for noncompliance and providing the required notification with the information required under (b)(3)(iii)(c).

f.title: Report withdrawal of an approved drug from sale within 30 calendar days (part 207 registrants)
f.statement: Within 30 calendar days of the withdrawal of an approved drug from sale, applicants who are manufacturers, repackers or relabelers subject to part 207 must submit, under 207.61 and 207.65, the NDC, the established and proprietary names, the NDA or ANDA number, and the date the drug is expected to be no longer in commercial distribution.

f.title: Submit information common to several applications only to the first approved application
f.statement: For all reports required by 314.81, the applicant shall submit information common to more than one application only to the application first approved, shall not report separately on each application, and shall identify all applications to which the report applies.

f.title: Code patient names instead of including names and addresses in reports
f.statement: Applicants should not include the names and addresses of individual patients in 314.81 reports; instead they should code the patient names whenever possible and retain the code in the applicant's files.

f.title: Keep enough patient identification for FDA to identify patients when needed
f.statement: The applicant shall maintain sufficient patient identification information to permit FDA, alone or with the investigator's records, to identify the name and address of individual patients; this ordinarily occurs only when FDA needs to investigate the reports further or has reason to believe they do not represent actual results.
